taxonomy_classification.classification_basis: Current-taxonomy review against VIGIL Failure Taxonomy 0.6.5 retains the occurrence as unclassified. The Compliance Logs Platform download endpoint outage makes observability classes materially relevant, but the preserved evidence does not establish their recognition conditions. VIGIL-FC-000044 Primary Evidence Accessibility Failure was tested, but no specific authoritative artefact required for a material governance review, authorised reviewer, or review question is shown to have been blocked by the endpoint outage. VIGIL-FC-000022 Material Event Non-Capture is not established because the record does not show that required events were never captured or retained. VIGIL-FC-000029 Execution-State Non-Disclosure is not established because the outage does not show a material task or tool execution state being withheld from a responsible supervisor. Loss of the download endpoint therefore remains an audit-plane service impairment rather than an asserted observability mechanism.

Accepted mappings: none. Rejected or not independently established: VIGIL-FC-000044: no occurrence-specific material review, required primary artefact and authorised reviewer are established; VIGIL-FC-000022: no evidence that events were not captured or retained; VIGIL-FC-000029: no material execution state is shown to have been withheld from a responsible supervision point. Primary classification changed: no — remains unclassified. Existing classifications retained: none. External-assessment material was checked where present or materially attributable in preserved sources; no external assessment was treated as automatic taxonomy evidence. Review used preserved canonical Incident evidence only and performed no new external research. Retained unclassified under taxonomy 0.6.5; audit-plane availability is evidenced, but the record does not establish the additional review or capture conditions required by current observability classes.
